absent: Queueing behavior, coupling algorithm and timing semantics beyond attribute meanings and stats layout.
Access-control enforcement, permission-check logic and locking.
Pulse event generation, wait and poll semantics, format conversion and kernel-consumer interaction.
Reservation state machine, transport handling and error recovery.
Process-control implementation semantics, privilege checks and argument validation.
Locking, concurrency and call-graph for all interfaces shown.

findings.text: Overload handling offers two modes with overflow as zero and drop as one, and early-drop handling offers dequeue-drop as zero and enqueue-drop as one; each group exposes a maximum one less than its private sentinel.

Congestion-notification classification uses a mask where low-latency ECT is one, classic ECT is two and any ECT is three, while segmentation handling uses zero for keep together and one for split; both groups expose a maximum one less than sentinel.

Queue attributes describe packet limit, byte memory limit, target and update intervals in microseconds, two rate factors scaled by 256, step thresholds in packets and microseconds, minimum length for step, coupling, overload and early selectors, classic protection percent, notification mask, segmentation flag and pad, with a maximum one less than sentinel.

Queue statistics carry current probability, classic and low-latency delays, per-queue input counts, maximum queue size, notification and step mark counts, a signed protection credit, and current, peak and limit memory values, all as fixed-width 32-bit fields.

Access-control constants reserve negative one for undefined identifier, use high bits to distinguish access versus default type, distinct low bits for user object, user, group object, group, mask and other tags, and classic read write execute permission bits with values four two one.

On-disk extended-attribute access-control form uses version two, a header holding a little-endian version word, and entries each holding little-endian tag and permission half-words plus a little-endian identifier word.

Portable fallback types define a descriptor set of 1024 bits stored as an array of longs sized by that constant, a signal-handler pointer taking an integer, and integer key and message-queue descriptor types.
Pulse interface reports a dotted version string, allows up to a few hundred sources, defines API version one as current, and limits device names to 32 bytes.

Pulse time uses signed seconds, signed nanoseconds and flags; kernel info pairs assert and clear sequence counters with two timestamps and a mode integer; kernel parameters pair API version and mode with assert and clear offsets; packed four-byte-aligned compat mirrors preserve field order.

Pulse mode bits select capture of assert, clear or both, request offset compensation per edge, advertise wait and poll capability, request echo of edges to output, select timespec versus NTP timestamp format, and identify kernel consumers for hard pulse with phase- or frequency-locked variants.
Pulse fetch bundles kernel info with a timeout timestamp, with a compat mirror using compat info and time; bind arguments carry timestamp format, edge selector and consumer selector as integers.

Pulse control uses five ioctls on one magic with small sequential numbers to get and set parameters, get capabilities, fetch data with timeout, and bind a kernel consumer with format, edge and consumer selectors.

Reservation status codes include success zero, generic error two, conflict hex eighteen, and three large path-failure codes, while reservation types enumerate six write-exclusive and exclusive-access variants covering plain, register-only and all-registrants scopes.

Reservation messages pass key plus type and flags for reserve and release, old and new keys with flags or type for register and preempt, key with flags for clear, and generation plus count plus pointer for reading keys versus key plus generation plus type for reading reservation; one flag bit ignores the existing key and key count is capped at 64K.

Reservation control uses eight ioctls on one magic numbered in the low two-hundreds to register, reserve, release, preempt, preempt-abort, clear, read keys and read reservation, with read variants returning data to the caller.

Early process-control numbers pair get and set operations for parent-death signal, dumpable, unaligned handling, keep-capabilities, floating emulation and exception masks, timing mode, process name, endian, secure computing, capability bounding set, timestamp counter, secure bits, timer slack, perf-event gating and machine-check kill policy, each with small documented subcodes.

Middle process-control numbers cover memory-map fields, tracer and subreaper flags, no-new-privs and thread-address query, huge-page disable, protection-key management, floating-point mode, ambient capabilities, vector lengths with inherit and on-exec deferral, speculation controls with per-threat selectors and enable states, authentication-key reset and tagged-address plus memory-tagging checks and masks.

Late process-control numbers cover I/O flusher state, syscall dispatch with off and exclusive versus inclusive enable plus allow-block filter values, enabled-key query, core-scheduling cookie operations with thread to process-group scopes, matrix lengths, write-execute denial, memory annotation and auxiliary-vector query, merge toggle, RISC-V vector and cache controls, and PowerPC DEXCR access.

Memory-map control structure carries 64-bit code, data, heap, stack, argument and environment bounds plus a user pointer to an auxiliary vector with its size and a descriptor backing the executable link.

Each header is guarded against reinclusion; maximum constants derive as sentinel minus one; compat pulse layouts preserve native field order with explicit packing; reservation 64-bit keys precede 32-bit type and flag words with explicit padding where needed.

Two headers define the same undefined identifier value so mixing them can collide; native versus compat pulse timestamps differ in alignment and must not be interchanged; reservation key reads use a user pointer plus count needing bounds checks; several process-control numbers use large magic values rather than small sequentials.
